elements.label: Reviewer
elements.description: Developer reviewing agent-written changes in Review Desktop; asks per-thread questions and watches agent turns.

elements.label: Coding agent
elements.description: The user's terminal coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor agent, or Pi) that authors reviews and answers review questions.

elements.label: Review Desktop
elements.description: Local desktop app plus its CLI and local server that turn agent-authored changes into guided Reviews and relay reviewer questions back into agent terminals.

elements.label: progressive-review package
elements.description: CLI, local server, and the native agent integration subsystem (install, launch, observe, attribute).

elements.label: Harness registry
elements.description: Maps install targets to launchable ReviewAgentHarness values and picks the preferred installed agent.

elements.label: preferredInstalledReviewAgent
elements.description: Selects the first installed launchable agent, preserving onboarding order.

elements.label: Install surface
elements.description: Installs skills and per-agent trace hooks; also the server-driven install status and removal path.

elements.label: runInstall
elements.description: Installs Review skills per target and configures agent lifecycle hooks for trace capture.

elements.label: CLI install service
elements.description: Server-side install status, apply, and removal; retires per-agent pieces when trace capture is disabled. Also exports the PATH shim writer reused by native terminals.

elements.label: Trace hook installation and parsing
elements.description: Installs session lifecycle hooks for Claude, Codex, and Pi, and parses agent trace formats for the trace subsystem.

elements.label: agent-trace-hooks
elements.description: Idempotent installers for Claude settings hooks, Codex config hooks, and the Pi extension.

elements.label: agent-trace-parser
elements.description: Sniffs and parses agent transcript JSONL into trace events.

elements.label: Authoring sessions
elements.description: Detects the invoking agent session from environment, freezes or forks it as the Review source session, and resolves fresh-harness fallbacks.

elements.label: authoring-session
elements.description: ReviewAgentHarness type (claude-code, codex, opencode, pi), SessionRef, session env detection (CODEX_THREAD_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, PI_SESSION_ID), and fresh-harness keys.

elements.label: createReviewSourceAgentSession
elements.description: Forks or freezes the invoking session per harness: native Codex fork, Claude transcript copy, Pi --fork, OpenCode session fork on a throwaway `opencode serve`.

elements.label: createTutorialAuthoringSession
elements.description: Runs one authoring turn per harness to seed the tutorial's genuine source session; OpenCode runs the turn through createOpencodeSession on a throwaway server, passing the session title and abort signal and returning only once the assistant has replied.

elements.label: Native agent bridge
elements.description: Models every harness as an AgentServer that launches terminals into sessions and streams session updates. Each harness has its own AgentServer class: Claude is observed through hooks posted to a loopback ingress plus transcript re-reads, Codex through the shared app-server's notifications, OpenCode through the HTTP API and SSE event stream of one Review-owned `opencode serve` process, and Pi through a bridge extension posting projections to a loopback ingress. Updates are mirrored into review threads.

elements.label: AgentServer contract
elements.description: native-session: the AgentServer interface (launch, updates, close), AgentServerOptions carrying the desktopEndpoint {baseUrl, token} that terminals use for thread lookups, LaunchInput, SessionSnapshot, the message.updated SessionUpdate, UpdatePipe shared by the server surface and the mirror, and NativeTerminalCommand, now derived from the protocol's openNativeAgentTerminal verb args. launch returns the reserved sessionId separately from the command that the desktop will run.

elements.label: LoopbackIngress
elements.description: loopback-ingress: a lazily started loopback HTTP listener (127.0.0.1, ephemeral port, per-listener random token checked via x-review-token) that a native terminal reports to. Posts to /<scope>/<sessionId> are dispatched to the owning server's onPost; bodies are size-capped JSON. Owned by ClaudeAgentServer (hooks) and PiAgentServer (bridge projections).

elements.label: ClaudeAgentServer
elements.description: claude-code: the AgentServer for Claude Code, simulated because Claude has no server of its own. Mints or resumes a session id, writes one shared observer-hook settings file (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd) in the runtime directory, and hands the terminal its per-session hook URL/token on its own LoopbackIngress plus the desktop thread URL/token. Each received hook re-reads the transcript on disk and fans the new tail out to subscribers, with delayed re-reads after turn-completing hooks. close() drains subscribers and shuts the ingress.

elements.label: CodexAgentServer
elements.description: codex: the AgentServer for Codex, built on the real app-server. Review owns one shared `codex app-server --listen` process through a CodexHost; launch starts or forks a thread on it (thread/start, thread/fork, or thread/resume for a resumed id), drives the review prompt with turn/start and waits for the thread to materialize, then hands the terminal `codex --remote <url> resume <threadId>` with env policy as inline TOML. updates seeds from thread/read and streams item/turn notifications; no transcript is read and no hooks are installed. close() closes subscribers and the host.

elements.label: OpencodeAgentServer
elements.description: opencode: the AgentServer for OpenCode, which is server-first (the TUI is a client of `opencode serve`). Review owns one such server through an OpencodeHost; launch creates a session (POST /session) in the review checkout, or looks up the source session through OpencodeClient.session and forks (POST /session/:id/fork) or resumes it inside that session's own project directory, because OpenCode sessions belong to a project keyed by directory; the session directory then scopes the prompt_async request and the terminal `opencode attach <url> --session <id> --dir <session directory>` with OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD plus the desktop thread URL/token. updates resolves a missing session directory through the same lookup, seeds from GET /session/:id/message, and follows the shared /global/event SSE stream: each event naming a known session triggers a re-read whose unseen messages fan out as message.updated. No transcript is read and no hooks are installed. close() closes subscribers, aborts the event stream, and closes the host.

elements.label: PiAgentServer
elements.description: pi: the AgentServer for Pi, whose server is an in-process extension. Mints or resumes a session id, launches pi with the pi-bridge-extension companion module and a per-session bridge URL/token on its own LoopbackIngress, and keeps the latest projection each bridge post carries, forwarding only the tail to subscribers. No transcript is read.

elements.label: terminal-command
elements.description: Shared launch helpers: env variable names (hook URL/token for Claude's ingress, bridge URL/token for Pi's ingress, thread URL/token for the desktop), ReviewCommandPath PATH shim, companion module resolution, the native hook shell command, and inline TOML serialization.

elements.label: native-hook-client
elements.description: Standalone hook relay run by Claude Code's settings hooks: posts the hook payload to the hook URL handed to the launch, which is the owning ClaudeAgentServer's LoopbackIngress. Env-gated and fail-open.

elements.label: NativeMessageMirror
elements.description: Subscribes to an AgentServer update pipe per thread binding and mirrors message.updated events into review thread storage, labelling messages per harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi).

elements.label: Codex app-server client and host
elements.description: codex-app-server: CodexAppServerClient speaks JSON-RPC over a pluggable Transport (stdio child or WebSocket via undici), with request, notify, and onNotification; CodexAppServerHost lazily spawns one shared `codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:0` child, exposes its URL and a reconnecting client, and kills it on close. startThread/forkThread run on a given client; startCodexThread/forkCodexThread open a one-off stdio client for callers outside the AgentServer.

elements.label: OpenCode serve host and client
elements.description: opencode: OpencodeClient speaks the `opencode serve` HTTP API with basic-auth password, directory-scoped requests (json over a private #fetch), a session(id) lookup that scans every worktree from GET /project for the one that serves GET /session/:id and returns the session with its directory, and a parsed /global/event server-sent-event generator; OpencodeServeHost reserves a loopback port, spawns one `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port <n>` child with a random OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD, polls /global/health until ready, and kills it on close. forkOpencodeSession and createOpencodeSession run on a throwaway host for callers outside the AgentServer (review source freeze and tutorial authoring); forkOpencodeSession resolves the source session first and forks within its project directory rather than the review checkout. createOpencodeSession submits the prompt with prompt_async and polls GET /session/:id/message once a second until an assistant message appears, honoring the caller's AbortSignal, failing on an assistant message that carries an error (assistantFailure), and giving up after a ten-minute deadline, because one model turn can outlast a single request timeout. projectOpencodeMessages maps session messages into review messages.

elements.label: Claude transcript reader
elements.description: Locates and projects Claude Code JSONL transcripts into review messages.

elements.label: pi-bridge-extension
elements.description: Companion module Pi loads in-process: on session_start, message_end, and agent_settled it projects the session manager's active branch into review messages and POSTs the whole projection to the bridge URL/token from its env. Fail-open. Bundled as its own tsdown entry.

elements.label: Local server surface
elements.description: Desktop session server: creates sessions, owns one AgentServer per harness, hosts the thread lookup route used by native agent terminals, and routes Review API verbs through it.

elements.label: desktop-server
elements.description: Global server: session registry, terminal-open relay to the desktop app, install status resolution, and the lazily created per-harness AgentServer map over the claude-code, codex, opencode, and pi modules (built with its own desktopEndpoint {baseUrl, token}) handed to each session handler and closed on shutdown. Hook ingress no longer lives here; the only native-agent-events route is the thread lookup, which asks every session handler's findAgentThread for the owning review.

elements.label: session-handler
elements.description: Per-session Hono handler; threads the agentServer factory from the global server into the review API and exposes the API's findAgentThread to the global hook routes.

elements.label: review-api
elements.description: Per-session API: resolves question routes (fork/resume/new), launches Ask-agent turns via AgentServer.launch, pairs the returned session identity with its terminal command for the desktop verb, feeds AgentServer.updates into message mirrors, and answers findAgentThread by matching a thread's bound agent session.

elements.label: Review thread store
elements.description: Persists review comment threads in review.mdx and exposes the `review threads` CLI the agent uses to read questions and post replies.

elements.label: appendReviewComment
elements.description: Appends a message to a review comment thread, carrying the message role and body format so agent replies are stored as agent responses.

elements.label: review threads CLI
elements.description: list/get/reply/resolve verbs over the thread store. `threads get` runs inside a native agent terminal and reads the attached thread from the desktop using the thread URL and the now-separate thread token env handed to the launch; `threads reply` is how the turn answers the reviewer.

elements.label: CLI runner
elements.description: Commander surface for review commands, including trace hook relays and runtime wiring.

elements.label: cli-runner
elements.description: Registers all review commands and their runtime implementations.

elements.label: review-protocol package
elements.description: Shared zod contracts between the CLI/server and the desktop app (verbs, sessions, install status).

elements.label: contracts
elements.description: Canonical schemas: AuthoringAgentSession and ReviewCommentAgentSession harness enums (claude-code, codex, opencode, pi), ReviewVerbRequest, install targets. The openNativeAgentTerminal verb carries session identity alongside a nested terminal command so desktop terminals can be keyed by the native session.

elements.label: Review Desktop shell
elements.description: VS Code fork hosting the review canvas, thread UI, and the terminals that run native agent turns.

elements.label: Terminal host
elements.description: Executes openNativeAgentTerminal verbs by reusing and focusing an existing terminal for the requested native session, or creating one from the nested command when none is live.

elements.label: reviewVerbs
elements.description: Verb sink for the desktop app: keys terminals by harness and session id, focuses a live terminal when reopening that session, otherwise creates one from the supplied command, and shows threads.

elements.label: Protocol mirror
elements.description: Desktop-side copy of the shared review-protocol schemas.

elements.label: reviewProtocol
elements.description: Mirrored zod schemas, kept in sync with review-protocol.
